column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|07-28|1804|Λούντβιχ Φόιερμπαχ|Ludwig Feuerbach|Ludwig Feuerbach was a German philosopher. In his book "The Essence of Christianity" he argued that God is a projection of human qualities, and he influenced Marx and Engels. He died in 1872.

bio|07-28|1866|Μπέατριξ Πότερ|Beatrix Potter|Beatrix Potter was an English writer and illustrator of children's books. She wrote and illustrated the story of "The Tale of Peter Rabbit" and of other animals. She bought land in the Lake District of the north and donated it to the National Trust. She died in 1943.

bio|07-28|1902|Καρλ Πόπερ|Karl Popper|Karl Popper was born in Vienna and lived in London. He was a philosopher of science. He argued that a theory is scientific when it can be falsified, and he wrote "The Open Society and Its Enemies". He died in 1994.

bio|07-28|1952|Μάχα Βαγιραλονγκόρν|Maha Vajiralongkorn|Maha Vajiralongkorn, also known as Rama X, is the king of Thailand. He ascended the throne in 2016, after the death of his father Bhumibol, and was crowned in 2019.

bio|07-28|1954|Ούγκο Τσάβες|Hugo Chávez|Hugo Chávez was a Venezuelan military officer and politician. He was president from 1999 until his death and promoted the "Bolivarian Revolution", with social programmes and strong confrontation with the United States. He died in 2013.

bio|07-28|2004|Φράνσις Κρικ|Francis Crick|Francis Crick was an English biologist and physicist. Together with James Watson he discovered the double helix of DNA in 1953, and the two shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1962. Later he studied the brain.

bio|07-29|1805|Αλεξίς ντε Τοκβίλ|Alexis de Tocqueville|Alexis de Tocqueville was a French historian and political thinker. His work "Democracy in America" analyses the institutions and equality in the United States, which he visited in 1831. He died in 1859.

bio|07-29|1856|Ρόμπερτ Σούμαν|Robert Schumann|Robert Schumann was a German Romantic composer. He wrote piano music, songs and symphonies, and he was married to the pianist Clara Schumann. In his last years he suffered from mental illness and died in an institution in 1856.

bio|07-29|1883|Μπενίτο Μουσολίνι|Benito Mussolini|Benito Mussolini was an Italian dictator. He founded the Fascist Party, governed Italy from 1922 and allied it with Hitler in the Second World War. He was killed in 1945 by Italian partisans.

bio|07-29|1890|Βίνσεντ βαν Γκογκ|Vincent van Gogh|Vincent van Gogh was a Dutch painter. He created works with vivid colours, such as "The Starry Night" and "Sunflowers", but he hardly sold a single painting while he was alive. He died in 1890 in France, after a gunshot.

bio|07-29|1905|Νταγκ Χάμαρσκελντ|Dag Hammarskjöld|Dag Hammarskjöld was a Swedish economist and diplomat. He served as Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1953. He was killed in 1961 in a plane crash in Zambia and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize posthumously.

bio|07-29|1981|Φερνάντο Αλόνσο|Fernando Alonso|Fernando Alonso is a Spanish racing driver. He won two Formula One World Championships, in 2005 and 2006 with Renault, and he remains active many years later.

bio|07-29|1983|Λουίς Μπουνιουέλ|Luis Buñuel|Luis Buñuel was a Spanish director and a pioneer of surrealism in cinema. He directed the films "An Andalusian Dog", "Viridiana" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie". He died in 1983.

bio|07-29|1994|Ντόροθι Κρόουφουτ Χότζκιν|Dorothy Crowfoot Hodgkin|Dorothy Crowfoot Hodgkin was a British biochemist. Using X-ray crystallography she determined the structure of penicillin and of vitamin B12, and in 1964 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

bio|07-30|1818|Έμιλι Μπροντέ|Emily Brontë|Emily Brontë was an English writer and poet. She wrote her only novel, "Wuthering Heights", which was published in 1847. She died young, in 1848, at the age of 30.

bio|07-30|1863|Χένρι Φορντ|Henry Ford|Henry Ford was an American industrialist and the founder of the Ford Motor Company. With the Model T and the assembly line he made the car affordable for many people. He died in 1947.

bio|07-30|1898|Όττο φον Μπίσμαρκ|Otto von Bismarck|Otto von Bismarck was a Prussian politician. As chancellor he united Germany in 1871 and for decades was the dominant diplomat of Europe. He resigned in 1890 and died in 1898.

bio|07-30|1912|Μέιτζι|Meiji|Meiji was Emperor of Japan from 1867 to 1912. During his reign the "Meiji Restoration" took place, and the country was modernised and became a great power. He died in 1912.

bio|07-30|1947|Άρνολντ Σβαρτσενέγκερ|Arnold Schwarzenegger|Arnold Schwarzenegger was born in Austria and became American. He was a bodybuilder, actor and politician. He became known with "The Terminator" and was governor of California from 2003 to 2011.

bio|07-30|1970|Κρίστοφερ Νόλαν|Christopher Nolan|Christopher Nolan is a British director. He has directed the films "Memento", the "Dark Knight" trilogy, "Inception", "Interstellar" and "Oppenheimer", which brought him his first Oscars.
bio|07-30|1974|Χίλαρι Σουάνκ|Hilary Swank|Hilary Swank is an American actress. She won two Oscars for Best Actress, for "Boys Don't Cry" and "Million Dollar Baby".
bio|07-30|1996|Κλοντέτ Κολμπέρ|Claudette Colbert|Claudette Colbert was born in France and was an American actress. She won an Oscar for "It Happened One Night" in 1934. She died in 1996.

bio|07-30|2007|Ίνγκμαρ Μπέργκμαν|Ingmar Bergman|Ingmar Bergman died in 2007 on the Swedish island of Fårö. He was a director and playwright, with films such as "The Seventh Seal", "Persona" and "Cries and Whispers".

bio|07-31|1784|Ντενί Ντιντερό|Denis Diderot|Denis Diderot was a French philosopher and writer of the Enlightenment. He was the publisher and chief editor of the "Encyclopédie", a collective effort to develop knowledge. He also wrote plays and novels.

bio|07-31|1875|Άντριου Τζόνσον|Andrew Johnson|Andrew Johnson was the 17th president of the United States. He became president after the assassination of Lincoln and was the first to undergo impeachment. He was acquitted by a single vote. He died in 1875.

bio|07-31|1886|Φραντς Λιστ|Franz Liszt|Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and virtuoso pianist of Romanticism. He created the symphonic poem and wrote major works for piano, such as the "Hungarian Rhapsodies". He died in 1886.

bio|07-31|1912|Μίλτον Φρίντμαν|Milton Friedman|Milton Friedman was an American economist. He led the Chicago School and supported free markets. In 1976 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics. He died in 2006.

bio|07-31|1914|Λουί ντε Φυνές|Louis de Funès|Louis de Funès was a French comic actor, known for his grimaces and his energy. He played in the films "The Gendarme of Saint-Tropez" and "La Grande Vadrouille". He died in 1983.
bio|07-31|1919|Πρίμο Λέβι|Primo Levi|Primo Levi was an Italian Jewish chemist and writer. He survived Auschwitz and wrote the book "If This Is a Man" about his experience. He died in 1987.

bio|07-31|1944|Αντουάν ντε Σαιντ-Εξυπερύ|Antoine de Saint-Exupéry|Antoine de Saint-Exupéry was a French pilot and the author of "The Little Prince". He disappeared on 31 July 1944 during a reconnaissance flight over the Mediterranean.

bio|07-31|1965|Τζ. Κ. Ρόουλινγκ|J. K. Rowling|J. K. Rowling is a British writer. She wrote the "Harry Potter" book series, published from 1997, which became one of the most successful in history, with films and a stage play.
bio|07-31|1989|Βικτόρια Αζαρένκα|Victoria Azarenka|Victoria Azarenka is a Belarusian tennis player. She reached first place in the world rankings and won two Australian Open titles, in 2012 and 2013.

bio|08-01|126|Πέρτιναξ|Pertinax|Pertinax was a Roman emperor in 193. He was the son of a freedman and came to the throne after the murder of Commodus, but he was killed by the Praetorian Guard after 87 days.

bio|08-01|1326|Οσμάν Α΄|Osman I|Osman I is considered the founder of the Ottoman Empire, from which the dynasty took its name. He led a small Turkish emirate in Bithynia. The exact date of his death is uncertain, and the first years of the dynasty are known mainly from later sources.

bio|08-01|1714|Άννα|Anne|Anne was Queen of Great Britain, the last of the Stuarts. During her reign, in 1707, England and Scotland were united and the War of the Spanish Succession was fought. She died in 1714, without surviving children.

bio|08-01|1744|Ζαν-Μπατίστ Λαμάρκ|Jean-Baptiste Lamarck|Jean-Baptiste Lamarck was a French biologist. He formulated one of the first theories of evolution, according to which the characteristics acquired by an organism are inherited. He also introduced the term "biology".

bio|08-01|1819|Χέρμαν Μέλβιλ|Herman Melville|Herman Melville was an American writer. He wrote "Moby-Dick", a novel about the hunt for a white whale, which was recognised as a masterpiece after his death. He died in 1891.
bio|08-01|1924|Αμπντουλάχ|Abdullah|Abdullah was King of Saudi Arabia from 2005 to 2015. He promoted limited reforms, such as the education of women. He died in 2015.
bio|08-01|1930|Πιερ Μπουρντιέ|Pierre Bourdieu|Pierre Bourdieu was a French sociologist. He developed concepts such as "cultural capital" and "habitus" and wrote "Distinction". He died in 2002.
bio|08-01|2005|Φαχντ|Fahd|Fahd was King of Saudi Arabia from 1982 to 2005. He was the first to use the title "Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques". His reign coincided with the Gulf War.

bio|08-01|2009|Κορασόν Ακίνο|Corazon Aquino|Corazon Aquino was a Filipino politician. She was President of the Philippines from 1986 to 1992 and led the country to democracy after the "People Power Revolution" against Marcos.

bio|08-02|1696|Μαχμούτ Α΄|Mahmud I|Mahmud I was an Ottoman sultan from 1730 to 1754. He came to the throne after the Janissary revolt that overthrew Ahmed III, and he worked to strengthen the army and fought a war with Persia.

bio|08-02|1921|Ενρίκο Καρούζο|Enrico Caruso|Enrico Caruso was an Italian tenor from Naples. He was one of the first to make recordings and is considered one of the greatest tenors of all time. He died in 1921, at the age of 48.

bio|08-02|1922|Αλεξάντερ Γκράχαμ Μπελ|Alexander Graham Bell|Alexander Graham Bell was born in Scotland and lived in Canada and the United States. He was an inventor and founded the Bell telephone company. He patented the telephone in 1876. He also worked in the education of the deaf.

bio|08-02|1923|Σιμόν Πέρες|Shimon Peres|Shimon Peres was an Israeli politician. He served as prime minister and as president of Israel. In 1994 he shared the Nobel Peace Prize with Rabin and Arafat for the Oslo Accords. He died in 2016.

bio|08-02|1923|Ουόρεν Χάρντινγκ|Warren G. Harding|Warren G. Harding was the 29th president of the United States, from 1921. His administration was marked by scandals, such as Teapot Dome. He died suddenly in 1923 while on a tour.

bio|08-02|1925|Χόρχε Ραφαέλ Βιδέλα|Jorge Rafael Videla|Jorge Rafael Videla was an Argentine general. He led the 1976 coup and was president of the junta until 1981. Thousands of dissidents disappeared during his time. He was convicted and died in prison in 2013.

bio|08-02|1932|Πίτερ Ο' Τουλ|Peter O'Toole|Peter O'Toole was an Irish actor. He became famous with the role of Lawrence of Arabia in 1962 and was nominated eight times for the Oscar without winning. He died in 2013.

bio|08-02|1934|Πάουλ φον Χίντενμπουργκ|Paul von Hindenburg|Paul von Hindenburg was a German field marshal in the First World War and President of Germany from 1925. He appointed Hitler chancellor in 1933. He died in 1934, and Hitler combined the offices.

bio|08-02|1942|Ισαμπέλ Αγιέντε|Isabel Allende|Isabel Allende was born in Peru and lived in Chile and the United States. She wrote the novel "The House of the Spirits", which belongs to magical realism. She is the niece of Salvador Allende.

bio|08-03|1811|Έλισα Ότις|Elisha Otis|Elisha Otis was an American inventor. He developed the elevator with a safety mechanism, which he demonstrated in 1854, and this helped build tall buildings. He founded the Otis company. He died in 1861.

bio|08-03|1872|Χάακον Ζ΄|Haakon VII|Haakon VII was the first King of Norway after the union with Sweden was dissolved in 1905. He was born a prince of Denmark. In the Second World War he resisted the Germans and went into exile. He died in 1957.

bio|08-03|1924|Τζόζεφ Κόνραντ|Joseph Conrad|Joseph Conrad was born in present-day Ukraine to Polish parents and wrote in English. He wrote "Heart of Darkness" and "Lord Jim", and he had earlier spent many years travelling as a sailor.
bio|08-03|1954|Κολέτ|Colette|Colette was a French writer. She wrote "Gigi" and "The Cat", with themes of love and women's freedom. She also had a career on the stage. She died in 1954.
bio|08-03|1963|Τζέιμς Χέτφιλντ|James Hetfield|James Hetfield is an American musician, the singer and rhythm guitarist of the band Metallica, which he founded in 1981 together with Lars Ulrich.
bio|08-03|1964|Αμπχισίτ Βετζάτζιβα|Abhisit Vejjajiva|Abhisit Vejjajiva is a Thai politician. He was prime minister of Thailand from 2008 to 2011, during a period of intense political conflict.

bio|08-03|1979|Εβάντζελιν Λίλι|Evangeline Lilly|Evangeline Lilly is a Canadian actress. She became known through the series "Lost" and appeared in the films "Ant-Man" and "The Hobbit", where she played Tauriel.

bio|08-03|2004|Ανρί Καρτιέ-Μπρεσόν|Henri Cartier-Bresson|Henri Cartier-Bresson was a French photographer. He was a pioneer of photojournalism, with the concept of the "decisive moment", and he co-founded the Magnum agency. He died in 2004.

bio|08-03|2008|Αλεξάντρ Σολζενίτσιν|Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn|Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn was a Russian writer. He wrote "One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich" and "The Gulag Archipelago" about the Soviet camp system. In 1970 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|08-04|1792|Πέρσι Σέλεϊ|Percy Bysshe Shelley|Percy Bysshe Shelley was born in 1792 in Sussex and was a Romantic poet. He wrote "Ozymandias" and "Ode to the West Wind", and he was a philhellene. He drowned in the Mediterranean in 1822.

bio|08-04|1859|Κνουτ Χάμσουν|Knut Hamsun|Knut Hamsun was a Norwegian writer. He wrote "Hunger" and "The Growth of the Soil", and in 1920 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. In the Second World War he supported the Nazis, which damaged his reputation.

bio|08-04|1875|Χανς Κρίστιαν Άντερσεν|Hans Christian Andersen|Hans Christian Andersen was a Danish writer. He wrote fairy tales such as "The Little Mermaid", "The Princess and the Pea" and "The Emperor's New Clothes". He died in 1875.

bio|08-04|1901|Λούις Άρμστρονγκ|Louis Armstrong|Louis Armstrong was born in New Orleans in 1901, although he himself said he was born in 1900. He was a jazz trumpeter and singer, with hits such as "What a Wonderful World". He died in 1971.

bio|08-04|1922|Ισμαήλ Εμβέρ|Enver Pasha|Ismail Enver Pasha was an Ottoman military officer and leader of the Young Turks. As minister of war he led the empire into the First World War. He was killed in 1922 in Central Asia, fighting against the Soviets.

bio|08-04|1948|Μιλέβα Μάριτς|Mileva Marić|Mileva Marić was a Serbian physicist and mathematician. She was the first wife of Albert Einstein, and they studied together in Zurich. She died in 1948. Her role in Einstein's work is debated but not documented.

bio|08-04|1960|Χοσέ Λουίς Ροδρίγκεθ Θαπατέρο|José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero|José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero is a Spanish politician. He was prime minister of Spain from 2004 to 2011, as leader of the Socialists. He supported, among other things, same-sex marriage.

bio|08-04|1961|Μπαράκ Ομπάμα|Barack Obama|Barack Obama was born in Honolulu. He was the 44th president of the United States, from 2009 to 2017, and the first African American to hold the office. In 2009 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|08-04|1997|Ζαν Καλμάν|Jeanne Calment|Jeanne Calment was a French woman who lived 122 years and 164 days. She is the person with the best-documented longevity in history. She was born in 1875 and died in Arles in 1997.

bio|08-05|1802|Νιλς Χένρικ Άμπελ|Niels Henrik Abel|Niels Henrik Abel was a Norwegian mathematician. He proved that the quintic equation cannot be solved by radicals and contributed to the theory of elliptic functions. He died young, in 1829, at the age of 26.
bio|08-05|1844|Ιλιά Ρέπιν|Ilya Repin|Ilya Repin was a Russian painter of realism. He painted "Barge Haulers on the Volga" and "The Zaporozhian Cossacks". He died in 1930 in Finland.

bio|08-05|1850|Γκυ ντε Μωπασσάν|Guy de Maupassant|Guy de Maupassant was born in 1850 in Normandy. He was a French writer and one of the greatest masters of the short story. He wrote "Boule de Suif". He died in 1893.

bio|08-05|1895|Φρίντριχ Ένγκελς|Friedrich Engels|Friedrich Engels was a German philosopher and businessman. He worked with Marx, with whom he wrote "The Communist Manifesto", and he wrote "The Condition of the Working Class in England" himself. He died in 1895.
bio|08-05|1930|Νιλ Άρμστρονγκ|Neil Armstrong|Neil Armstrong was an American astronaut. On 20 July 1969, as commander of Apollo 11, he became the first person to walk on the Moon. He died in 2012.

bio|08-05|1962|Μέριλιν Μονρόε|Marilyn Monroe|Marilyn Monroe was an American actress and a symbol of Hollywood. She starred in the films "Some Like It Hot" and "Gentlemen Prefer Blondes". She died in 1962, at the age of 36.

bio|08-05|1968|Μαρίν Λε Πεν|Marine Le Pen|Marine Le Pen is a French far-right politician. She led the National Front, which was renamed the National Rally, and she stood as a candidate for the French presidency in 2012, 2017 and 2022.

bio|08-05|1984|Ρίτσαρντ Μπάρτον|Richard Burton|Richard Burton was a Welsh actor. He played in the films "Cleopatra" and "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?" and was married twice to Elizabeth Taylor. He died in 1984.
bio|08-05|2000|Άλεκ Γκίνες|Alec Guinness|Alec Guinness was an English actor. He won an Oscar for "The Bridge on the River Kwai" and played Obi-Wan Kenobi in "Star Wars". He died in 2000.

bio|08-06|1637|Μπεν Τζόνσον|Ben Jonson|Ben Jonson was an English writer and a contemporary of Shakespeare. He wrote comedies such as "Volpone" and was the first official poet of the English court. He died in 1637.

bio|08-06|1660|Ντιέγο Βελάθκεθ|Diego Velázquez|Diego Velázquez was a Spanish Baroque painter and court painter of Philip IV. He painted "Las Meninas" and the portrait of Pope Innocent X. He died in 1660.
bio|08-06|1809|Άλφρεντ Τέννυσον|Alfred Tennyson|Alfred Tennyson was an English poet of the Victorian era. He wrote "Idylls of the King" and "In Memoriam" and served as poet laureate. He died in 1892.

bio|08-06|1881|Αλεξάντερ Φλέμινγκ|Alexander Fleming|Alexander Fleming was a Scottish biologist. In 1928 he discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic, and in 1945 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Florey and Chain. He died in 1955.

bio|08-06|1911|Λουσίλ Μπολ|Lucille Ball|Lucille Ball was an American actress and comedian. She starred in the series "I Love Lucy", one of the most successful television series in history, and with her husband she founded the Desilu company. She died in 1989.

bio|08-06|1928|Άντι Γουόρχολ|Andy Warhol|Andy Warhol was an American artist and a leading figure of Pop Art. He became known for images of Campbell's soup cans and for portraits of Marilyn Monroe. He died in 1987.

bio|08-06|1969|Τέοντορ Αντόρνο|Theodor Adorno|Theodor Adorno was a German philosopher and sociologist, a member of the Frankfurt School. Together with Horkheimer he wrote the "Dialectic of Enlightenment". He died in 1969.

bio|08-06|1973|Φουλχένσιο Μπατίστα|Fulgencio Batista|Fulgencio Batista was a Cuban military officer and dictator. He was overthrown by Fidel Castro's Cuban Revolution on 1 January 1959. He lived in exile and died in Spain in 1973.

bio|08-06|1983|Ρόμπιν Φαν Πέρσι|Robin van Persie|Robin van Persie is a former Dutch footballer who played as a forward. He played for Arsenal and Manchester United and was the Premier League's top scorer. He later became a coach.

bio|08-07|317|Κωνστάντιος Β´|Constantius II|Constantius II was a Roman emperor and a son of Constantine the Great. After his father's death he shared the empire with his brothers and from 353 ruled alone. He supported Arianism. He died in 361.

bio|08-07|1848|Γιενς Γιάκομπ Μπερζέλιους|Jöns Jacob Berzelius|Jöns Jacob Berzelius was a Swedish chemist. He established the symbols of the chemical elements using Latin letters and discovered selenium, thorium and cerium. He was one of the founders of modern chemistry.

bio|08-07|1876|Μάτα Χάρι|Mata Hari|Mata Hari was a Dutch dancer. During the First World War she was accused in France of spying for the Germans and was executed in 1917. The evidence against her is disputed, and the matter is still discussed.
bio|08-07|1921|Αλεξάντρ Μπλοκ|Alexander Blok|Alexander Blok was a Russian poet of Symbolism. He wrote the poem "The Twelve", about the October Revolution. He died in 1921, at the age of 40.

bio|08-07|1938|Κονσταντίν Στανισλάφσκι|Konstantin Stanislavski|Konstantin Stanislavski was a Russian actor and director. He founded the Moscow Art Theatre and developed the "Stanislavski system" of acting, which deeply influenced theatre and cinema.

bio|08-07|1941|Ραμπιντρανάθ Ταγκόρ|Rabindranath Tagore|Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali poet and philosopher. He wrote the poetry collection "Gitanjali" and in 1913 became the first non-European to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He also wrote the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.
bio|08-07|1958|Μπρους Ντίκινσον|Bruce Dickinson|Bruce Dickinson is an English singer, the lead vocalist of Iron Maiden since 1981. He is also a pilot and a writer.

bio|08-07|1966|Τζίμι Γουέιλς|Jimmy Wales|Jimmy Wales is an American businessman. In 2001, together with Larry Sanger, he co-founded Wikipedia, the free online encyclopedia, and he founded the Wikimedia Foundation.

bio|08-07|1975|Σαρλίζ Θερόν|Charlize Theron|Charlize Theron was born in South Africa. She is an actress and producer. She won the Oscar for Best Actress for "Monster" in 2003 and starred in "Mad Max: Fury Road".

bio|08-08|117|Τραϊανός|Trajan|Trajan was a Roman emperor from 98 to 117. He was born in Spain. Through his conquests, especially of Dacia, the empire reached its greatest extent. He died in Asia Minor.

bio|08-08|1827|Τζωρτζ Κάνινγκ|George Canning|George Canning was a British politician and prime minister for a few months in 1827. As foreign secretary he supported the Greek revolutionaries and contributed to the London Protocol of 1826. He died in office.

bio|08-08|1879|Εμιλιάνο Ζαπάτα|Emiliano Zapata|Emiliano Zapata was a Mexican revolutionary. He led the agrarian movement in the Mexican Revolution, with the slogan "Land and Liberty". He was assassinated in 1919.
bio|08-08|1898|Εζέν Μπουντέν|Eugène Boudin|Eugène Boudin was a French painter. He painted the beaches of Normandy and was a forerunner of Impressionism and a teacher of Claude Monet. He died in 1898.

bio|08-08|1902|Πολ Ντιράκ|Paul Dirac|Paul Dirac was an English physicist. He developed quantum mechanics and formulated the Dirac equation, which predicted the existence of antimatter. In 1933 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Schrödinger. He died in 1984.

bio|08-08|1937|Ντάστιν Χόφμαν|Dustin Hoffman|Dustin Hoffman is an American actor. He played in the films "The Graduate", "Kramer vs. Kramer" and "Rain Man", and the last two won him Oscars for Best Actor.

bio|08-08|1964|Τζουζέπε Κόντε|Giuseppe Conte|Giuseppe Conte is an Italian lawyer and politician. He was prime minister of Italy from 2018 to 2021, heading coalition governments, and later became leader of the Five Star Movement.

bio|08-08|1981|Ρότζερ Φέντερερ|Roger Federer|Roger Federer is a former Swiss tennis player. He won 20 Grand Slam tournaments, with eight titles at Wimbledon, and he stayed at the top of the world rankings for almost 310 weeks. He retired in 2022.
bio|08-08|2010|Πατρίσια Νιλ|Patricia Neal|Patricia Neal was an American actress. She won an Oscar for "Hud" and appeared in "Breakfast at Tiffany's" and "The Fountainhead". She died in 2010.

bio|08-09|1516|Ιερώνυμος Μπος|Hieronymus Bosch|Hieronymus Bosch was a Dutch painter. He became known for his fantastical and monstrous works, such as "The Garden of Earthly Delights", with religious and moral themes. He died in 1516.

bio|08-09|1776|Αμεντέο Αβογκάντρο|Amedeo Avogadro|Amedeo Avogadro was born in 1776 in Turin. He was an Italian chemist and physicist. Avogadro's law and Avogadro's number bear his name. He died in 1856.
bio|08-09|1896|Ζαν Πιαζέ|Jean Piaget|Jean Piaget was a Swiss psychologist. He studied how children's thinking develops and described the stages of cognitive development. He died in 1980.

bio|08-09|1919|Ερνστ Χέκελ|Ernst Haeckel|Ernst Haeckel was a German biologist and naturalist. He supported Darwin's theory in Germany and introduced the term "ecology". He also made detailed drawings of marine organisms. He died in 1919.

bio|08-09|1938|Ότο Ρεχάγκελ|Otto Rehhagel|Otto Rehhagel is a German football coach. As coach of the Greek national team he won Euro 2004 in Portugal, one of the greatest achievements in Greek sport. Earlier he had won the league with Werder Bremen.

bio|08-09|1939|Ρομάνο Πρόντι|Romano Prodi|Romano Prodi is an Italian politician and economist. He was prime minister of Italy and president of the European Commission, from 1999 to 2004, when the great enlargement of the EU took place.
